Fixes #333042

## Problem

The Integrated Browser spellchecks editable fields (red underlines), but the custom context menu never reads `params.misspelledWord` / `params.dictionarySuggestions`. Right-clicking a misspelled word only shows Cut / Copy / Paste / Inspect.

## Change

When the click is on a misspelled word:
- Prepend Chromium's suggestions (`webContents.replaceMisspelling`)
- Offer **Add to Dictionary** only when `session.isPersistent()` is true (ephemeral sessions used for untrusted workspaces / `workbench.browser.dataStorage: ephemeral` cannot persist that API)
- Omit an empty spelling section when there are no suggestions and the dictionary item is hidden

Inspect / Add Element to Chat are unchanged.

## How to test

1. Open an editable page in the Integrated Browser (trusted workspace, default storage).
2. Type a misspelled word so it gets a red underline.
3. Right-click the word.
4. Confirm suggestions appear above the edit items, clicking one replaces the word, and **Add to Dictionary** clears the underline.
5. Right-click a correctly spelled word and confirm the extra items are absent.
6. Repeat in an untrusted workspace or with `workbench.browser.dataStorage: ephemeral`. Confirm suggestions still work and **Add to Dictionary** is not shown.

⚠️ Security fixes

High severity

  • GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272: malformed qualified private Cache-Control directives could cause cross-user information disclosure in shared caches or a parse-time crash. The cache parser now treats empty qualified directives conservatively and safely handles mixed qualified and unqualified directives. Fixed by 9f10f1e9, with regression coverage in 466e99d1.

Medium severity

  • GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5: a malicious type property on a duck-typed blob-like HTTP/1.1 request body could inject CRLF sequences into the generated content-type header. Undici now coerces and validates the value before adding it to the request. Fixed by 33928bc2.
  • GHSA-jr45-8vmc-qm54: optional whitespace around = in qualified no-cache and private directives could bypass shared-cache restrictions and disclose authenticated data across users. Cache-Control parsing now normalizes these forms and applies conservative cache decisions. Fixed by 98011a86.
  • GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524: the retry interceptor could expose a stale Content-Length after resuming a partial response, potentially causing downstream response desynchronization, hangs, or corruption. Undici now rejects partial responses whose Content-Length is inconsistent with Content-Range. Fixed by 1b5a5312, with corrected fixtures in 4a9dafb1.
  • GHSA-v3r7-h72x-cjcm: unsanitized domain and unparsed values passed to setCookie() could inject cookie attributes. Undici now validates cookie domains, paths, and unparsed attributes more strictly. Fixed by 3bf91ddb.

## The problem

The agent host filter (the host picker on vscode.dev/agents) assumed **one provider = one host**. `AgentHostFilterService` turned every registered remote agent-host provider into exactly one picker entry, and `SessionsList.update()` scoped the list with `session.providerId === selectedProviderId`.

Cloud sandboxes broke that assumption. `CloudSandboxAgentHostContribution._ensureProvider` registers one provider **per sandbox environment** (`agenthost-cloudsandbox__<envId>`), and Mission Control creates one session per environment. So a user with 20 tasks got 20 picker entries, each showing exactly one session — burying the tunnel machines the picker exists to switch between.

The conceptual mismatch: a picker entry meant two things at once — *which machine am I connected to* (identity) and *which sessions do I see* (scope). For tunnels those are 1:1. A sandbox is a per-session ephemeral box, so the 1:1 assumption collapses.

Knock-on effects from the same root cause:
- Default selection could land on a sandbox — `_validate` fell back to `hosts[0]` sorted alphabetically, so a fresh vscode.dev profile could open scoped to a random task's ephemeral environment.
- `Manage Remote Agent Hosts…` listed every sandbox as a removable host.
- `WebWorkspacePicker` scoped new-session workspaces to a single entry, so "new session" targeted one sandbox.

Desktop was unaffected — `_applyHosts` only computes a selection when `isWeb`.

## The change

Decouple "connection" from "picker entry" via a new `IAgentHostGroup`. Each sandbox keeps its own provider and connection (one address, one credential set, one session-type authority), but providers sharing a group id fold into **one** filter entry.

- **`IAgentHostGroup`** (`sessions/common/agentHostSessionsProvider.ts`) — a provider may declare `hostGroup: { id, label, icon?, order?, connectable? }`. Tunnels/WSL/SSH omit it and keep the existing 1:1 mapping.
- **`IAgentHostFilterEntry`** gains `id`, `providerIds`, `icon`, and `connectable`. `AgentHostFilterService._rewatchProviders` buckets by `hostGroup?.id ?? provider.id` and rolls up member status (a group reads connected if any member is).
- **Selection is set-based** — `selectedProviderId` → `selectedHostId` + `selectedHost`. Consumers scope by the entry's whole `providerIds` set.
- **Cloud sandboxes declare the group** — `{ id: 'cloudsandbox', label: 'Cloud Sandboxes', icon: package, order: 1, connectable: false }`. `connectable: false` because a sandbox connects when one of its sessions is opened, so a connect/disconnect toggle would act on nothing the user pointed at.

Collateral fixes in the same change:
- `_validate` prefers the first **connectable** entry, so a fresh profile can't default into the sandbox group. (Worth noting: "Cloud Sandboxes" sorts before "Host A" alphabetically — only this rule keeps the default off it. There's a test for exactly this.)
- The connect/disconnect button is hidden and the "(disconnected)" menu suffix dropped for non-connectable entries — a group of 12 sandboxes reading "disconnected" looked broken.
- Grouped members are excluded from `Manage Remote Agent Hosts…` — you can't meaningfully "remove" a sandbox; discovery would just recreate it.
- `WebWorkspacePicker` shows recents across all group members but no "Select Folder…" for a group, since there's no single machine to browse.

## Migration

The persisted storage key is unchanged and now holds an entry id. A stale `agenthost-cloudsandbox__<envId>` value simply fails validation and falls through to the connectable-first fallback — no migration code needed.

## Reviewer notes

- **`_rewatchProviders` autorun**: `connectionStatus.read(reader)` is the unconditional first statement of every loop iteration, so no provider can drop out of the autorun's dependency set when grouping short-circuits.
- **Not done here**: the cleaner "one aggregate sandbox provider fanning out over N connections" refactor. Session ids, resource schemes, and chat content-provider registration are all derived per connection authority inside the 5.3k-line `BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider` — high risk, and not needed to fix this.

## Validation

- Typecheck clean (apart from two pre-existing errors in `assignmentService.ts`, a file this PR doesn't touch)
- ESLint clean, layers check clean, hygiene clean
- `agentHostFilterService.test.ts` — 12/12 pass, including 5 new tests covering folding, status rollup, `selectedHost.providerIds`, reconnect/disconnect fan-out, and the connectable-first fallback

**Still needs a CI run**: the browser-harness suites (`cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts`, `tunnelAgentHost.contribution.test.ts`, sessionsList tests) import CSS/DOM and couldn't be driven from Node locally.

The sessions list hover in the Agents window gave no indication that a session was picked up from another application, and no way to reach the setting that governs whether those sessions appear at all. This adds a trailing, separated **External Session** row that links to that setting.

The row shows only when `ISession.isExternal` is set, and behaves like the other hover links — activating it opens the settings editor revealing `chat.agentSessions.showExternal`.

### Changes

- **`sessionSummaryHover.ts`** — new optional `externalSession` field on `ISessionSummaryHoverData`, rendered as a final `.session-summary-hover-section`. Sections already carry a `border-top`, so the separator comes for free; reusing `_appendButtonRow` gives the row the same link styling, hover color and focus outline as `Created by`.
- **`sessionHoverContent.ts`** — the Agents-window adapter populates the field from `session.isExternal`, opening the setting via `IPreferencesService.openSettings({ jsonEditor: false, query: '@id:chat.agentSessions.showExternal' })`, matching how other chat surfaces reveal a single setting.
- **`sessionsList.ts` / `openSessionLinkOpener.contribution.ts`** — thread `IPreferencesService` through the row renderer and the session-pill hover provider, which share the adapter.
- **Tests / fixture** — coverage that an external session's row targets the right setting query and a local session has none, plus a `SessionHover_ExternalSession` component fixture.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Fix authentication redirect loop · Claude │
│ Workspace · ~/projects/vscode            │
│ Branch · main                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ⧉ External Session                       │  ← clickable, opens Settings
└────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Notes for review

- The setting is read through the existing `ChatConfiguration.ShowExternalAgentSessions` constant rather than a literal, so the `@id:` query stays in sync.
- `isExternal` is read when the hover content is built; `setupDelayedHover` re-invokes the factory on each hover, so this matches the other non-reactive fields (`title`, `changes`).
- The row is intentionally added in the shared adapter, so the `agent-host-session://` pill hover in chat output picks it up too.

chat: show one OS notification when a session has no more work

Agent host sessions can be open in the editor window and the agents window at the
same time. This caused two problems with the OS notifications. A "finished" toast
came when a response ended, even if more requests were in the queue. A session that
was open in two windows made one toast from each window.

- Adds an idle observable in the chat window notifier. It combines the request
  state, the input state, and the count of queued requests. The notifier shows the
  toast only when the session has no more work. A 500ms delay prevents a toast in
  the short gap between two queued turns.
- Makes the chat window notifier the only source of toasts in a window. It now
  shows the toast for needed input and for the idle state. The toast in the chat
  accessibility service is removed. That service keeps the accessibility signal and
  the ARIA announcement.
- Limits the sessions window notifier to sessions that have no chat model in this
  window. Sessions with a model are the responsibility of the chat window notifier,
  which knows about the queue.
- Adds a dedupe key to the toast options. The main process does not show a second
  toast while a toast with the same key is on the screen. This prevents duplicate
  toasts from two windows for one session.
- Delays the toast 250ms in a window that does not show the session. The window
  that shows the session makes its toast first, so a click opens the window that
  the user worked in.
- Delays the completed toast 1500ms in the sessions window notifier. A session with
  no chat model here gives no queue information, so the delay prevents a toast in
  the gap between two queued turns. See
  https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/issues/426 for the permanent fix.

## Summary

Fixes **Open in Editor** for Agent Host sessions running in a Dev Container. The action now translates the Agent Host workspace URI into the `vscode-remote://dev-container+...` URI expected by the Dev Containers extension.

Follow-up to #331934.

Tracking issue: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/317380

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Use `dev-container+`, not `attached-container+`**: These sessions originate from a local source folder with a Dev Container configuration. Encoding that source folder lets the Dev Containers extension rediscover the configuration and reconnect using its normal resolver path.
- **Carry the source host folder explicitly**: The runtime Dev Container connection now retains `hostPath`; the container ID alone is not sufficient to construct a `dev-container+` authority.
- **Preserve the container workspace path**: Only the URI scheme and authority are translated. The Agent Host's remote path (for example `/workspaces/project`) remains the folder opened inside the container.
- **Match the extension's authority encoding**: The host path is UTF-8 hex encoded, matching `getDevContainerUri`. This safely preserves POSIX paths, Windows drive-letter paths, spaces, and explicitly supported WSL UNC paths.
- **Do not claim generic UNC-share support**: Dev Containers explicitly routes `\\wsl.localhost` / `\\wsl$` paths through WSL, while ordinary network-share UNC support is not reliable end to end.
- **Code OSS testing limitation**: The marketplace Dev Containers extension intentionally does not register its resolver without the Microsoft-only `vsda` dependency. The exact generated URI was therefore validated separately in official VS Code Insiders rather than bypassing that product check.

</details>

## Changes

- Retain the original local source folder on managed Dev Container Agent Host connections.
- Resolve Dev Container session workspaces to `vscode-remote://dev-container+<hex-host-path>/<container-path>`.
- Share Agent Host folder URI translation between remote provider types and the Open in Editor action.
- Add regression coverage for POSIX, Windows drive-letter, and WSL UNC source paths.

## What changed
- Present the parent session row using the canonical main chat status while preserving aggregate session status for filtering, lifecycle, notifications, and flat lists.
- Show non-main chat **Input Needed** state, pulse, title emphasis, and reduced-motion fallback on the owning nested chat row.

## What

Fixes two independent bugs that broke the "Sent from another chat" / "Sent by another session" request-origin link (the small pill shown above a delegated chat request, linking back to the chat/session that sent it).

## Why

1. **Agents window** — `OpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution` fell back to a bare `openSession()` when the link carried no chat id. Per `buildOpenSessionLinkUri`'s documented invariant, an absent chat id means "the session's default chat," but `openSession()` only activates the session without switching the active chat. So clicking the pill was a no-op whenever a *different* chat of the same session (e.g. a peer/subagent chat) was already showing — exactly the case when a delegated request originates from the session's default chat.
2. **Regular editor window** — `AgentHostOpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution` only registered an opener with `IOpenerService` (for markdown-authored links), never with `IChatRequestOriginService` (which is what the pill's click handler actually calls). So clicking the pill found no opener and fell back to treating the opaque `agent-host-session://` link as a session resource directly, which never resolves.

## Fix

- `OpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution._open()` now always resolves a concrete target chat — the peer chat when a chat id is present, otherwise the session's `mainChat` — and opens it uniformly via `ISessionsService.openChat()`.
- `AgentHostOpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution` now also registers a request-origin opener that reuses its existing link-opening logic.

## Testing

- Added a regression test for each fix, reproducing the exact metadata shape captured from a live repro (delegation link with no chat id, and a request-origin link opened from the editor window).
- Updated an existing test that encoded the old (buggy) "no chat id → openSession" expectation.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, and `npm run hygiene` all pass clean.

## Summary

Prevents an asynchronous Agent Host customization refresh from publishing into a session that was removed while customization discovery was still pending.

## Symptom

Recent Code - Insiders Agent Host logs contained warnings such as:

```text
2026-08-25 16:02:20.956 [info] [Copilot] Chat created; its backing stays deferred until the first send: copilotcli:/9d927329-1762-430f-a91b-a10ca927afcf
2026-08-25 16:02:23.072 [warning] [AgentHostStateManager] Action for unknown session: copilotcli:/9d927329-1762-430f-a91b-a10ca927afcf, type=session/customizationsChanged
```

The warning means a provider-side customization refresh produced a state action after the target session had already left the state manager.

## Root cause

`AgentSideEffects._publishSessionCustomizations` reads the session's current customizations, awaits `agent.getChatCustomizations(...)`, and then compares the newly resolved set against the current session state before dispatching `session/customizationsChanged`.

Previously, both reads used optional chaining directly on `getSessionState(...)`. This collapsed two distinct states to the same value:

- an existing session whose customizations have not been published yet; and
- a session that was removed while discovery was pending.

Both yielded `undefined`. Consequently, if the session disappeared during the `await`, the existing deduplication/supersession logic could still reach `dispatchServerAction` and emit an action for an unknown session.

## Fix

- Require the session to exist before starting customization discovery.
- Recheck that it still exists after the asynchronous discovery completes.
- Preserve the existing structural deduplication and superseded-refresh retry behavior for live sessions.

The guard is intentionally at the asynchronous producer rather than in `AgentHostStateManager`: unknown-session warnings remain useful for finding other stale producers, while this refresh simply has no valid target after removal.

## Test coverage

Adds a regression test that:

1. starts customization discovery;
2. waits until discovery is pending;
3. removes the session from the state manager;
4. completes discovery; and
5. verifies that no `SessionCustomizationsChanged` envelope is emitted.

agentHost: keep a model reference for chats that are created

A side chat that was started with `/btw` during an active turn opened an empty widget that
never answered. `createSideChat` acquired a chat model, applied the carried-over model and
agent, then released the reference immediately. The reference count fell to zero, which
disposed the provided session and released its agent host chat subscription. The open and
send steps that followed raced that asynchronous teardown. Both steps resolved the session
content at the same time and each built an `AgentHostChatSession`. The second session
replaced the first in `_activeSessions`, but the chat model kept the first. Turn progress
went to a session that no widget observed.

- Deduplicates concurrent session resolution in `ChatSessionsService`. Callers share one
  in-flight promise. The shared work is cancelled only after every caller cancels, so one
  caller that gives up cannot abort the work of the others.
- Disposes a session that the service does not adopt. This covers the session that loses the
  cache race and a session that a provider returns after cancellation. The agent host
  provider does not honour cancellation, so it can still return a fully wired session.
- Replaces the immediate release in `createSideChat`, `forkChat`, and `_createAdditionalChat`
  with a model reference that expires after 10 seconds. The reference keeps the model alive
  across the open and send steps and cannot become permanent.
- Removes the redundant `getOrCreateChatSession` call from those three paths. The standard
  `acquireOrLoadSession` path resolves the session and owns it with a reference count.
- Logs an error when a new agent host session replaces an active session for one resource.
  This invariant was assumed in many places but was enforced in none.

## Problem

Custom agents can choose a model in an `.agent.md` file, but they cannot currently choose that model's reasoning effort.

The Copilot SDK already supports a per-agent `reasoningEffort` setting. However, when VS Code converts an `.agent.md` file into the SDK configuration, it does not forward the `reasoning-effort` frontmatter value. As a result, this configuration is silently ignored:

```yaml
---
name: quick-explorer
model: gpt-5
reasoning-effort: low
---
```

This makes it difficult to give lightweight agents a faster default while allowing more complex agents to use deeper reasoning.

## Fix

This change:

- reads `reasoning-effort` from custom-agent frontmatter;
- accepts `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`;
- forwards supported values to the Copilot SDK as `CustomAgentConfig.reasoningEffort`;
- leaves the property unset when it is missing or unsupported, preserving existing behavior;
- intentionally forwards `max` even though the pinned SDK type declaration has not caught up with runtime support;
- registers the field with the `.agent.md` language service so the key and all five values have completions without an unsupported-attribute diagnostic; and
- documents the new frontmatter option.

This is a per-agent default only. It does not add a dynamic reasoning-effort override to individual subagent calls.

Lets someone already signed in to Microsoft reach Copilot without a second trip through the browser. The `microsoft` provider already holds an Entra token; this trades it for a GitHub one.

## How the flow works

Two exchanges, on purpose.

The first buys a `read:user` discovery token, just enough to call `GET /user` and find out which GitHub account the Entra identity maps to. That account is shown to the user, and nothing is published until they confirm it. The second exchange then mints the scopes the caller actually asked for.

The discovery token is never persisted and never published as a session. Neither token is ever logged.

## What survives a reload

Entra-brokered sessions live in memory for the life of the window and never touch the Keychain. What persists is the user's consent: a row in global state holding the GitHub account label, the Microsoft account label, and the GitHub user id. A fresh window mints the session again from that row without prompting, re-running discovery to confirm the row still points at the same account.

Rows are keyed by GitHub account label, because that is what VS Code itself keys an account by. `getAccounts` collapses sessions by label and the account preference is stored by label. A session read back from the Keychain can carry a placeholder id, an old numeric one, or one from a lookup that failed, so the id is no way to tell two accounts apart. The id has exactly one job here: checking that the token GitHub just returned belongs to the account the row names, which a label cannot do because logins get renamed and freed logins get taken.

## Signing out

Signing out of GitHub drops the row. Signing out of Microsoft drops the sessions, since nothing can renew them, but deliberately leaves the rows alone.

That asymmetry matters. The Microsoft account list is a per-window cache that legitimately reads empty for a moment while it repopulates, and the rows are global state shared by every window. Acting on a blink of that list would sign the user out everywhere with no way back. Dropping only the in-memory sessions self-heals: the next read mints them again from the row that is still there. Getting it wrong costs one round trip instead of the account.

## Testing

37 unit tests pass across `accountLinks.test.ts`, `entraTokenExchange.test.ts`, `flows.test.ts`, plus the workbench tests in `chatSetup.test.ts` and `defaultAccount.test.ts`. End to end this was exercised through sign in, window reload, cross-window sign in from the Agents window, and both sign-out paths.

Swift's regex literal syntax (e.g., `/\//`) causes VS Code to incorrectly append `// ` on Enter when the cursor is on a line containing `//` inside a regex or string — not in an actual line comment.

## Changes

- **`extensions/swift/language-configuration.json`**: Tighten the `onEnterRules` `beforeText` pattern from `\/\/.*` to `^\s*\/\/.*`, anchoring the match to the start of the line so the rule only fires for actual line comments, not embedded `//` in strings or regex literals.

```swift
// Before: pressing Enter here incorrectly prepends "// " on the new line
let _ = someStrings.map { $0.replacing(/\//, with: "") }
//                                      ^^ triggers false positive

// After: only lines where // begins the comment trigger the rule
// this is a real comment   ← still works correctly
let _ = someStrings.map { $0.replacing(/\//, with: "") }  ← no longer triggers
```

Addresses #261660.

Related Electron issue: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/42378

## Why

VS Code dynamically disables Electron background throttling while a chat request is running. If the request begins after the window has already been hidden or minimized, Electron can leave `RenderWidgetHostImpl`, `RenderWidgetHostViewAura`, `DelegatedFrameHost`, and `FrameEvictor` with inconsistent visibility state.

This was reproduced from a VS Code source build without an extension by applying the following sequence directly to the main `BrowserWindow`:

1. Start with background throttling enabled.
2. Minimize the window and wait for the hidden transition to complete.
3. Call `webContents.setBackgroundThrottling(false)` while minimized.
4. Restore the window.

Leaving throttling disabled reproduced the blank window. A transient `false -> true` sequence before restore also reproduced intermittently, showing that setting the value back to `true` does not reliably repair visibility state already corrupted by the hidden transition.

The resulting behavior matches #261660: the renderer remains interactive, resizing or minimizing/restoring recovers presentation, and the issue can recur. It also matches the failure mechanism documented in electron/electron#42378.

The dynamic throttling path was introduced in #254827 shortly before the first reports in #261660. Because Electron does not currently provide an application-level transition that reliably repairs this state across hidden, minimized, and native occlusion cases, this change removes the dynamic setter path and leaves Electron at its default background-throttling behavior.

## Trade-off

This removes the workaround added for #252384, so renderer-side chat work may again be throttled while the window is backgrounded. That is preferable to risking loss of the entire window presentation. A future Electron fix for electron/electron#42378 could allow the original behavior to be restored safely.

## Overview

## What changed

- **Fix stale row height for approvals that change while a chat row is virtualized offscreen.** The per-row approval autorun is tied to the row template, which is disposed when the row scrolls offscreen. If an approval then appears, clears, or changes line count, the ListView kept the row's stale cached height, and on re-entry the renderer re-seeded its height baseline from the new state — so the first autorun emitted no height update and the blocking "Allow" control could be clipped by `overflow: hidden`.

  `SessionsList` now owns an autorun (`reconcileChatApprovalHeights`) that watches each chat's live approval and reconciles its cached height via the tree delegate, **independent of whether the row is currently rendered**. Height updates applied to offscreen elements correct the ListView's cached size, so the row shows the right height (and never clips the Allow control) when scrolled into view. The autorun is re-established after every `update()` because chat items are rebuilt each render.

- **Accessibility: keep the one-time permission scope in the Allow button's accessible name** — `Allow: {0}` → `Allow once: {0}`. Simultaneously visible Allow buttons still get a distinct accessible name (the command they approve), and now retain the "once" semantics.

## Why not reconcile during render instead

A render-time reconcile was considered and rejected: firing the height change synchronously during `renderElement` re-enters the tree's render/transaction (`Error: Already in transaction`), and a deferred fire cannot be distinguished from the tree's own ambient re-render in tests. Tracking heights outside the rendered-template lifetime (a list-owned autorun) corrects the cache synchronously on the model change and is deterministically testable.
